version_tag: #141 CARRIER CHAIN v17 rev B — altitudes corrected. Satellites now sit at assy 9.5 / 14.5 / 19.5 (was 9.5/14.0/18.5) on the 5.0mm band pitch. rev A had a second, quieter fault beyond the boss collision: the arm's riser shoulder sat ON TOP of the plate, so the satellite above seated 0.5mm HIGHER than its sun ball band — the mesh lamina and the band would have been on different levels. The pad is now budgeted into the pitch: 0.20 clearance over the spinning satellite below + 1.30 plate + 0.50 pivot pad + 3.00 satellite = 5.00. Without a pad the satellite rubs the plate's whole top face across its r17 lamina — friction at the worst radius; with it, it bears on a r3.5 collar at its own pivot. ALSO FIXED: the arm plate was 24 overlapping SOLID cylinders swept between the stations plus a separate bore annulus at the from-station — the sweep's first cylinder sits exactly there, so the union filled the bore back in and the arm had NO HOLE to press onto the post. Plate is now one plane polygon with a real interior ring. The 1.0mm sun spacer is emitted from the generator now; it was hand-built for rev A with no source, so nobody could have regenerated it for this change. Press fits unchanged: arm bores 2.60 onto design-2.70 posts (prints 2.64) = 0.04 interference, expect to tap. Gates: arms clear the rotating satellite below by 0.20mm each, both satellites seat exactly on their bands, arm2 grips 1.30mm of arm1's post, fingers clear the sun slim core by 0.61mm radially. 4 parts, flat, no supports, xy-comp -0.06. | QUIET.
